events.quote: On March 20, 2023, during a quality check at a vehicle assembly plant, it was noticed that a second row seat head restraint on a Model Year 2023 BMW X5 had difficulty locking in position.
An engineering review was initiated and, on March 21st, the seat supplier was contacted.
A review of supplier production and process information was performed.
It was found that, due to a production control system issue, the End-of-Line (EOL) validation process needed to be bypassed for a limited time period.
As a result, seats may have been assembled with suspect head restraint guide sleeves during this time period.
Further reviews were conducted involving images captured during the seat production and assembly process, and other production and assembly quality information.
A containment action was performed, and head restraints were also physically examined.
Quality checks of other vehicles with various build configurations and option packages were also performed.

An analysis of the information identified potentially affected seats, and also confirmed that potentially affected seats were only those equipped with head restraint guide sleeves during the production process deviation time period.
Vehicle assembly information and supplier production and process records were reviewed to determine the number, and production dates, of potentially affected vehicles.
On March 30, 2023, BMW determined that affected vehicles may not conform to FMVSS 202a Section 4.2.6, and decided to conduct a voluntary non-compliance recall.

events.quote: In May 2018, Super Products was notified by a customer that a tank strap tie rod had disengaged from the top of a Mud Dog vehicle, and the water tank strap had fallen down.
In July 2019, Super Products received a similar report from a customer for a Camel vehicle.
The Mud Dog and the Camel are the only two Super Product models that use this tank tie rod part.
Super Products instituted a design change on August 1, 2019, to increase rod penetration and weld size for the tank strap tie rod on both models.
The last of these incidents occurred in May 2022 while the Camel vehicle was operating on a public road and the tank strap fell and came into contact with the back window of another vehicle.
This caused property damage to the other vehicle, but no accident or injury.
Super Products then examined other Camel and Mud Dog vehicles that were manufactured around the same time period as the 6 reported cases.
Super Products examined 129 additional tank tie rods on 32 vehicles.

As a result of the investigation, one additional vehicle was identified on which the tank tie rod had been replaced with a threaded rod, but Super Products could not confirm if the original tank tie rod had disengaged before the repair with the threaded rod was made.
Also, through the course of the investigation, Super Products discovered cracked welds on 9 tank tie rods, but none of the rods were disengaged.
All 9 cracked tank tie rods were replaced.
On March 31, 2023, Alamo decided to declare a voluntary safety recall to remedy this issue.
Between January 2020 and June 2022, Super Products learned of 4 more incidents of tank strap tie rod weld failures for the affected vehicle population.

After the May 2022 incident, Super Products conducted metallurgical tests on the tank tie rod and the connected square tabbed washer to confirm the cause as insufficient rod penetration and weld size.
In October 2022, during the course of the investigation a customer reported another disengaged tank tie rod.

Dec 2022 and ongoing, REV Recreation Group and Lippert started an investigation and reviewed testing data to determine the effect of consumers adding an aftermarket drop hitch.

In May of 2023, REV Recreation Group notified Lippert that a risk to safety may occur on certain Lippert manufactured hitches and that REV Recreation Group would immediately conduct a recall out of an abundance of caution on behalf of the hitch supplier.
A review of warranty history revealed no other reported failures of this part as of this time.
